title: Pentagon Seeks Additional $200 Billion to Fund Iran War
partialText: The request, which the White House has not submitted to Congress, is already encountering some resistance.

title: Trump Says U.S. and Qatar Not Involved in Strike on Iran’s South Pars Gas Field
partialText: President Trump said Israel was responsible for the attack, but vowed to “massively” destroy the gas field if Tehran hit Qatar’s energy facilities in retaliation.

title: The Effects of High Oil Prices
partialText: Our chief economics correspondent, Ben Casselman, breaks down how gasoline prices have responded to the oil crisis in the Persian Gulf, and what is in store for inflation if the price of oil remains above $100 per barrel.

title: The Abuse Allegations Against a Civil Rights Icon, and a 48% Rise in Oil Prices
partialText: Plus, there’s a big catch for that stunning ocean view.

title: ‘Go Big and Go Loud’: Inside the Justice Dept.’s Push to Prosecute Protesters
partialText: Prosecutors have struggled to prove in court what the president and his aides have repeatedly said in public: that a network of leftist activists presents a serious threat to national security.

title: Trump Vowed to Crack Down on Fraudsters, but He’s Pardoned Dozens
partialText: Across both of his terms, President Trump has granted clemency to more than 70 allies, donors and others convicted in fraud cases.

title: ‘We’re Just Seen as Sex Objects’: Dolores Huerta’s Years in the U.F.W.
partialText: The co-founder of the United Farm Workers talked about her relationship with Cesar Chavez, and the night he raped her.

title: More Cesar Chavez Fallout Expected After Sex Abuse Accusations
partialText: Some states and cities have canceled their observances of Cesar Chavez Day on March 31. Los Angeles leaders said they planned to change the holiday to “Farm Workers Day” and untether it from Mr. Chavez’s birthday.

title: Cesar Chavez, a Civil Rights Icon, Is Accused of Abusing Girls for Years
partialText: An investigation by The New York Times found extensive evidence that the United Farm Workers co-founder groomed and sexually abused girls who worked in the movement.

title: Chavez’s Tarnished Legacy
partialText: We look at a major Times investigation into a labor rights icon.

title: How Did Flea Make a Jazz Album? Practice, Practice, Practice.
partialText: The Red Hot Chili Peppers bassist returned to the trumpet, for a new record featuring Nick Cave, Thom Yorke and a core cast of contemporary jazz luminaries.

title: How Japan’s Leader Sanae Takaichi Found Her Voice in D.C. Decades Ago
partialText: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi got her start in politics as an intern for a trailblazing Colorado lawmaker. She returns to Washington this week to meet with President Trump.

title: Trump’s Friendship With Japan’s Leader Takaichi Faces Test Over Iran
partialText: In Washington on Thursday, President Trump is expected to press Sanae Takaichi for military help in the Strait of Hormuz. But she faces constraints on what she can offer.

title: Iran War Narrows Fed’s Path to a Rate Cut
partialText: Jerome H. Powell, the Fed chair, wants to keep the central bank’s policy options open as officials stare down another economic shock that threatens to stoke inflation and crimp growth.

title: In This Crisis, the Best Investors Can Expect From the Fed Is Nothing
partialText: A rate cut in the next few months could signal major problems in the economy.

title: The Markets Contend with Powell’s Long Goodbye at the Fed
partialText: The chair of the Federal Reserve said that he might not leave the central bank any time soon, setting up a potential clash with President Trump.

title: A.I. Bots Can Act as Personal Digital Assistants, but There Are Serious Risks
partialText: New A.I. bots can do more than just chat. They can edit files, send emails, book trips and cause trouble.

title: Sorry, Mom. You’re Chatting With an A.I. Agent, Not Your Son.
partialText: Silicon Valley’s young coders are getting creative with this new technology. They also worry they’re not spending enough time with it.

title: The Soldier Who Came Back From the Dead
partialText: Told that Nazar Daletskyi had died, his Ukrainian family buried what they thought were his remains. He turned up three years later in a prisoner-of-war exchange.

title: A Crucial Loan for Ukraine Becomes Election Leverage for Orban
partialText: European leaders are pushing Prime Minister Viktor Orban to stop blocking a €90 billion loan to Kyiv. But the issue is a rallying cry in elections in Hungary set for April 12.

title: Elon Musk Whips Up Frenzy Against John Thune Over SAVE America Act
partialText: The billionaire Elon Musk is furiously pushing on social media for Senator John Thune, the majority leader, to pass the SAVE America Act. But so far, he hasn’t publicly spent money to promote the bill.

title: The Wealthy House Candidate With a History of Bawdy Facebook Posts
partialText: The social media habits of Peter Chatzky, a tech executive who is running to unseat Representative Mike Lawler in New York, show a penchant for crude jokes.

title: She Killed a Family With Her Speeding Car. Is Probation Enough?
partialText: Two years ago, an older driver killed a couple, their toddler and their baby as her vehicle sped through San Francisco. A judge has indicated that he intends to let her avoid prison, home detention and community service.

title: The Weather Is Getting Wilder, and Some See a Dire Signal in the Data
partialText: Several of the Earth’s systems are changing faster than predicted as global temperatures rise, scientists say.

title: California Probably Hasn’t Seen the Worst of This Week’s Heat Wave
partialText: Wednesday was the hottest March day ever in many cities across California, Nevada and Arizona. Phoenix recorded its earliest 100-degree day.

title: New Museum Debuts New Building With Ambitious ‘New Humans’
partialText: It’s a big, serious, adult show worth debating and even fighting over — just the way our critic likes it.

title: Trump’s Hypocrisy on Religious Freedom
partialText: Republicans’ attacks on Islam are shameful and full of lies.

title: White Identity Is Galvanizing the Right
partialText: He wrote a book on anti-white bias. The White House noticed.

title: Ozempic Is About to Go Generic in India, China and Canada
partialText: In India, China and several other nations, Novo Nordisk is on the verge of losing patent protection for its blockbuster weight loss drug, opening the door for cheaper competing versions.

title: Home Health Care Aides Say It’s Time to End ‘Inhumane’ 24-Hour Shifts
partialText: The aides want the New York City Council to pass a law that would limit their shifts to 12 hours, except in the case of emergencies.

title: In Swaths of Germany, the Far-Right AfD Is Part of the Fabric
partialText: The Alternative for Germany party, or AfD, is shunned in federal politics but is a regional force. This fall, it could win broader power for the first time.

title: The New Alzheimer’s Blood Tests: What to Know
partialText: The tests could help to improve dementia care, but scientists say there are still some caveats and unknowns.
